statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of six representative paths and all 58 catalog checks.

page.notes: Public, multilingual adult-media catalog. Templates represented: category index, category listing, video detail/player, contact/legal content, RTL locale, and unknown-route recovery. Not covered: every category/video/locale duplicate template, destructive/commercial/account flows because none are exposed, and playback completion beyond initial embedded-player availability.

paths.description: Homepage category index, representing entry and broad category discovery.
Teen (18+) category listing, representing the repeated thumbnail-grid/listing template and browse journey.
Representative video detail/player page, covering the primary content-consumption task and related-content template.
Contact/legal support surface, checked for forms, reporting routes, and content structure.
Arabic localized category route, representing non-Latin and right-to-left localization.
Unknown URL recovery path, used to inspect HTTP and user-visible failure handling.

findings.summary: The fixed dark palette does not respond to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Computed-style probes under light and dark preferences both returned body background rgb(20, 21, 24), body text rgb(139, 141, 164), and color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation and menu state changes swap abruptly.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition usage; the interaction video shows the custom mobile menu appearing/disappearing without a state transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions and a reduced-motion-safe state transition for the menu.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide no position-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: After scrolling to 1200px, the header remained position: static and its top was -1200px; CSS contained no scroll-state or scroll-progress technique.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep essential navigation available with a restrained sticky/shrinking header or add a lightweight scroll-position affordance.

findings.summary: Category and detail pages do not visibly identify the current page or guide attention after navigation.
findings.evidence: DOM and Lighthouse evidence found zero headings on category/detail templates; screenshots show a grid or player with no visible page title, breadcrumb, selected category, or directional cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a descriptive H1/current-location cue and preserve clear focus/attention after navigation.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation toggle is an ad-hoc span and does not expose open state.
findings.evidence: The menu probe found SPAN role=button, no aria-expanded, and a manually shown .navigation-row; there is no button, popover, dialog, or details primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real button with aria-controls/aria-expanded and a semantic disclosure or popover pattern with keyboard/light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: The card grid adapts only through viewport breakpoints, not component-level conditions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero @container/container-type rules and ten physical left/right declarations; reused thumbnail cards are controlled by global media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a size container for reusable grids/cards and adapt card content with container queries while retaining a fallback.

findings.summary: Many category links and the menu control are too small for reliable touch input.
findings.evidence: At 360px, the probe found numerous tag links only 15px high and a 26x26 menu control, although keyboard focus remained visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary controls, without making the text itself oversized.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs silently become the homepage instead of showing a recoverable not-found state.
findings.evidence: The HTTP probe requested /this-route-does-not-exist-audit and received a final 200 homepage; the screenshot and DOM contained no error explanation or recovery choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 status and a concise not-found page with Home, Categories, and retry/search choices.

findings.summary: The detail template shifts because thumbnail space is not reserved.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured CLS 0.105 and identified the thumbnail list and unsized images as culprits; the image primitive found 92/92 images without width and height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and keep placeholder geometry identical to final media geometry.

findings.summary: Thumbnail links and embedded frames lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and frame-title; 90 detail links had no accessible name, 90/92 images lacked alt, and the player iframe title was empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every thumbnail link a concise content name, meaningful images useful alt text, and each player/ad iframe a descriptive title.

findings.summary: The main content has no main landmark or heading hierarchy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main on both templates; the DOM probe found no headings and only header/nav/footer landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main and add one descriptive H1 followed by a logical heading hierarchy; retain visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Dense tag text is cramped and difficult to scan.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot shows long comma-separated labels clipped to one line; computed target rectangles show many links rendered at only 15px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase line-height and spacing, expose concise primary titles, and move secondary tags into a readable wrapping or disclosure treatment.

findings.summary: Reflow works, but touch targets and embedded media equivalents are inadequate.
findings.evidence: 360px layout had no overflow and allows scaling, but many links are 15px high and the cross-origin player iframe has no title or visible caption/equivalent metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the good reflow while enlarging hit areas and supplying titled, caption-capable media with a text description where needed.

findings.summary: Metadata is generic and duplicated across distinct content.
findings.evidence: The category and detail use the same “Teen (18+) - Collider Porn” title and generic “ColliderPorn Free Sex Videos free” description; the detail has no visible content title.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate unique titles/descriptions from the actual category or video entity and align them with a visible H1.

findings.summary: Crawlable thumbnail URLs have no descriptive link text.
findings.evidence: The URLs are real href links and the viewport is valid, but Lighthouse found repeated unnamed image links and the detail probe counted 90 links without names.
findings.suggestedFix: Put descriptive text or an accessible name in each content link so users, crawlers, and agents can understand its destination.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are undermined by a missing sitemap and soft-404 behavior.
findings.evidence: Canonical and hreflang links exist and pages return 200, but /sitemap.xml returns 404 and an invented URL resolves to the homepage with status 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap covering canonical localized routes and return 404/410 for missing content rather than a soft 404.

findings.summary: Video and category entities have no structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph properties on a representative video detail page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching the visible content and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Cookies and transport policy are not securely hardened.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but all six observed first-party cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None; the auth-like id cookie also lacked HttpOnly. CSP and HSTS were absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, appropriate SameSite, and HttpOnly flags; deploy HSTS and a tested CSP.

findings.summary: Identifiers and third-party advertising cookies are set without an evident consent choice.
findings.evidence: Six first-party identifiers were present, including 365-day cid/181dbb cookies; Lighthouse saw third-party cookies from the player/ad stack, while load screenshots showed no consent control.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise identifiers, defer non-essential third parties until valid consent where required, and offer an equally prominent reject/manage choice.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The core video player disappears when JavaScript is disabled.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML preserves listing text, but the no-JS detail screenshot shows an empty player rectangle because the iframe src is a javascript: location replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a normal HTTPS iframe/source or noscript fallback so the primary media/link remains available without client scripting.

findings.summary: Missing routes are concealed as successful homepages.
findings.evidence: The unknown route followed to the homepage with HTTP 200 and no error state, retry, or explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve explicit 404/500/offline states with useful recovery actions and preserve the requested context.

findings.summary: The Arabic locale is marked ar but rendered left-to-right.
findings.evidence: The Arabic route reported html lang=ar, no dir attribute, computed body direction=ltr, zero logical CSS properties, and ten physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl for Arabic and other RTL locales, migrate layout spacing/positioning to logical properties, and test mirrored navigation.

findings.summary: Tracking defaults are not transparent or reversible on arrival.
findings.evidence: Persistent identifiers and third-party cookies were observed before any visible consent or preference controls appeared.
findings.suggestedFix: Use privacy-protective defaults and an honest consent/preferences surface with clear purpose, reject, change, and withdrawal controls.

findings.summary: The thumbnail catalog lacks responsive, modern image delivery.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 92/92 images without srcset, 26 legacy JPEG/PNG assets, no modern formats, and 87 below-fold images not marked lazy in the scanned state.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, dimensions, and native lazy loading for below-fold thumbnails.

findings.summary: The player brings a third-party advertising/cookie footprint without an explicit user choice.
findings.evidence: The detail HAR reached xvideos.com and Lighthouse observed cookies/requests from xvideos and advertising hosts; the page itself offers no media/privacy controls beyond the embedded player.
findings.suggestedFix: Load third-party media only when needed, use privacy-enhanced embedding where possible, and gate non-essential ad/analytics requests behind consent.

Secure cookies, consent, and browser policies
Fix the no-JS player and real HTTP error recovery
Reserve image space and modernize responsive image delivery
Correct RTL direction and logical layout
Add unique metadata and rich video/category signals
Improve mobile controls and semantic navigation
Add restrained position and transition guidance
Reduce third-party and media resource cost
